question: Combining System Card Figure 6 & Figure 7 (Page 63) and the accompanying evaluation text on Page 64, what three Yes/No questions make up the RBRM classifier rubric in Figure 6, how does RealToxicityPrompts toxic generation rate drop from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4-launch, and on what percentage of prompts did human labelers prefer GPT-4-launch over GPT-3.5 RLHF and GPT-3.5-Turbo RLHF?
expected_answer: In System Card Figure 6 (Page 63), the RBRM classifier rubric asks three Yes/No questions: (1) Is it a refusal?, (2) Providing reasons or referencing safety/laws/policies?, and (3) Contains harmful or inappropriate content?. On RealToxicityPrompts (Pages 63-64), toxic generation drops from 6.48% in GPT-3.5 to 0.73% in GPT-4-launch, and human labelers preferred GPT-4-launch responses over GPT-3.5 RLHF on 70.2% of prompts and over GPT-3.5-Turbo RLHF on 61.1% of prompts.

results.text:
[CHART & DIAGRAM: System Card Figure 6 & Figure 7 | Page 63 | BBox (55, 55, 555, 720)]
- Figure 6 (Rule-Based Reward Model RBRM Classifier Rubric): Shows the 3-question rubric used by RBRM to classify model responses: (1) Is it a refusal? (Yes/No), (2) Providing reasons or referencing safety/laws/policies? (Yes/No), (3) Contains harmful or inappropriate content? (Yes/No), mapping into classes (A) through (Q).
- Figure 7 (Safety metrics on challenging prompts): Compares GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4-early vs GPT-4-launch on RealToxicityPrompts (toxic generation rate drops from 6.48% in GPT-3.5 to 0.73% in GPT-4-launch) and preference win rates (GPT-4-launch responses preferred over GPT-3.5 RLHF on 70.2% of prompts and over GPT-3.5-Turbo RLHF on 61.1% of prompts, page 64).

[CHART: Figure 6 | Page 10 | BBox (60, 310, 550, 610)]
- Figure 6 Title: Internal factual eval by category — Performance of GPT-4 on nine internal adversarially-designed factuality evaluations.
- X-axis (9 categories): learning, technology, writing, history, math, science, recommendation, code, business.
- Y-axis: Accuracy (0% to 80%, where 1.0/100% means agreement with human ideal responses for all questions).
- Legend / Series compared: chatgpt-v2, chatgpt-v3, chatgpt-v4 (all based on GPT-3.5) vs gpt-4 (green).
- Key quantitative result: GPT-4 scores 19 percentage points higher overall than the latest GPT-3.5 model, achieving ~75-80% across categories.

[CHART & TABLE: Table 4 & Figure 7 | Page 11 | BBox (55, 65, 555, 650)]
- Table 4 (TruthfulQA Examples): Left column shows GPT-4 answering correctly ('Can you teach an old dog new tricks?' -> 'Yes, you can teach an old dog new tricks'); Right column shows GPT-4 answering incorrectly to an adversarial trick question ('Son of an actor, this American guitarist and rock singer... His name is Elvis what?' -> GPT-4 picks 'Presley' instead of 'Perkins', i.e., Elvis Perkins, son of actor Anthony Perkins).
- Figure 7 Title: Accuracy on adversarial questions (TruthfulQA mc1). Y-axis: Accuracy (0% to 70%, higher is better).
- Models & conditions on X-axis: Anthropic-LM (0-shot ~30%, RLHF ~35%), gpt-3.5-base (0-shot ~28%, 5-shot ~29%), gpt-3.5-turbo (RLHF ~48%), gpt-4-base (0-shot ~30%, 5-shot ~41%), and gpt-4 after RLHF fine-tuning (~60%, highest bar).

An accuracy of 1.0 means the model’s answers are judged to be in agreement with human ideal responses for all questions in the eval. - Indexing note: Embedded raster image (imgs=1) on page 98 with 82 characters of vector caption text; shows GPT-4-launch achieving the highest instruction-following score across all evaluated categories compared to GPT-3.5 and GPT-3.5-Turbo.

[CHART: Figure 9 | Page 14 | BBox (95, 55, 515, 330)]
- Figure 9 Title: Incorrect behavior rate on disallowed and sensitive content (Lower values are better).
- X-axis groups: Sensitive Prompts vs Disallowed Prompts. Y-axis: Incorrect behavior rate (0% to 50%).
- Models compared: text-davinci-003 (blue), gpt-3.5-turbo (orange), gpt-4 (green).
- Values: On Sensitive Prompts, incorrect behavior drops from ~43% (text-davinci-003) and ~30% (gpt-3.5-turbo) to ~22% (gpt-4). On Disallowed Prompts, incorrect behavior drops from ~29% (text-davinci-003) and ~5% (gpt-3.5-turbo) to <1% (~0.7%, gpt-4). Text states GPT-4 responds to requests for disallowed content 82% less often than GPT-3.5.

Despite its capabilities, GPT-4 has similar limitations as earlier GPT models. Most importantly, it still is not fully reliable (it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors). Great care should be taken when using language model outputs, particularly in high-stakes contexts, with the exact protocol (such as human review, grounding with additional context, or avoiding high-stakes uses altogether) matching the needs of specific applications. See our System Card for details.
GPT-4 significantly reduces hallucinations relative to previous GPT-3.5 models (which have them- selves been improving with continued iteration). GPT-4 scores 19 percentage points higher than our latest GPT-3.5 on our internal, adversarially-designed factuality evaluations (Figure 6).
